column1: Combine the grated Parmigiano and water in a large pan and heat slowly to 176°F (80°C), never letting it exceed 194°F (90°C).
Once the cheese turns stringy, take the pan off the heat and let it cool to room temperature.
Reheat to 176°F (80°C) one more time, then let it cool again.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight, until it separates into three layers.
Spoon off the creamy top layer and reserve it as Parmigiano cream. Strain the liquid middle layer to use as stock and discard the solids at the bottom.
For the pepper distillate, crush all the peppers, vacuum-seal them with the water, and leave at 68°F (20°C) for 24 hours.
Distill the infused liquid in a rotary evaporator at 75°F (24°C), then transfer it to a spray bottle and keep cool.
Warm the Parmigiano stock in a saucepan.
Toast the rice with a little olive oil in a separate pan.
Add the warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring and letting each addition absorb before adding the next.
When the rice is about three-quarters cooked, start stirring in spoonfuls of Parmigiano cream along with some of the black pepper oil.
As the rice nears doneness, work in the remaining cream and pepper oil.
Take the pan off the heat and keep stirring for 1 minute while it rests.
Spread the risotto flat on a plate and mist it with the pepper distillate before serving.
